examples.question_text: Triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(0,0)$, $B(2,4)$ and $C(6,2)$. Calculate the gradients of its sides and hence identify its right angle.

Find the side lengths of each triangle and classify it as equilateral, isosceles or scalene.

a. $A(-2,0)$, $B(2,0)$, $C(0,2\sqrt3)$.

b. $D(0,0)$, $E(2,3)$, $F(4,0)$.

c. $G(0,0)$, $H(3,0)$, $J(1,2)$.
examples.solution_text:
a.

$\begin{aligned}AB&=\sqrt{(2-(-2))^2+(0-0)^2}=4\\BC&=\sqrt{(0-2)^2+(2\sqrt3-0)^2}=\sqrt{4+12}=4\\AC&=\sqrt{(0-(-2))^2+(2\sqrt3-0)^2}=4\end{aligned}$

All three sides are equal, so $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.

b.

$\begin{aligned}DE&=\sqrt{(2-0)^2+(3-0)^2}=\sqrt{13}\\EF&=\sqrt{(4-2)^2+(0-3)^2}=\sqrt{13}\\DF&=\sqrt{(4-0)^2+(0-0)^2}=4\end{aligned}$

Exactly two sides are equal, so $\triangle DEF$ is isosceles.

c.

$\begin{aligned}GH&=\sqrt{(3-0)^2+(0-0)^2}=3\\HJ&=\sqrt{(1-3)^2+(2-0)^2}=2\sqrt2\\GJ&=\sqrt{(1-0)^2+(2-0)^2}=\sqrt5\end{aligned}$

All three lengths are different, so $\triangle GHJ$ is scalene.

c. Use diagonal gradients to explain why it is not a square.
